newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil power firm profits soar in 1996 - study.
newsitem.headline: Brazil power firm profits soar in 1996 - study.

text.p: Profits at Brazilian electrical utilities soared 1,574 percent in 1996 from the prior year due to rate hikes and restructuring in the sector, a study by a local market consultant said.
A spokesman at Tecnica Assessoria de Mercado de Capitais e Empresarial said the report also found return on equity at power firms jumped to two percent last year from 0.10 percent in 1995.
"It happens that 1995 was a mediocre year and many firms posted losses," he said. "In 1996, fewer companies had losses and profits were higher."
The top-gaining power firm was federal power holding he said, citing the study.
The study also showed earnings rose 148 percent at Sao Paulo state power firms, 298 percent at Rio de Janeiro state companies and 86.5 percent at Parana state-owned firms, he said.
Market analysts and traders said the soaring profits last year and in 1997's first quarter are behind a bull run in Brazilian power stocks this year.

The Sao Paulo bourse' Electrical Energy Index of nine most-liquid power shares has risen 79.3 percent in nominal terms to end Tuesday at 3,478 points, compared with a 78.7 percent hike in the bolsa's Bovespa index.

In its study, Tecnica surveyed the financial results of the 177 companies from all sectors using figures not adjusted for inflation and converted to dollars using the exchange rate at the close of the period.
Profits among those firms, including industrial firms, banks and electrical utilities, surged to to a total $8.3 billion in 1996, up 163.7 percent from $3.1 billion the prior year.
Excluding the massive losses reported by federal bank Banco do Brasil, profits at the surveyed firms totalled $10.2 billion last year, up 69 percent from $6.0 billion in 1995, the official said.
